meta.caveat_greedy_policy: This table was played by the greedy policy — the one that loses two games in three to the search. That measurably moves the order: on this same field 3 of 12 decks change tier, and Quest Hunter falls from S to D. Decks that reward sequencing are marked down here. Recompute with the “search” policy to see the other order.
meta.caveat_noisy: At {games} games per pair a single matchup carries roughly ±{margin} points of noise, which is wider than the tier bands. Treat this run as a shape, not a ranking — raise the games per pair to narrow it.
meta.caveat_not_ladder: This is the simulator playing itself, not the ladder. TavernLab does not scrape HSReplay or Untapped for winrates, so it cannot tell you what is strong in ranked play.
meta.caveat_scripted_ai: The AI is scripted. Combo and value-engine decks come out below their real strength; treat their numbers as a lower bound.
meta.caveat_search_policy: This table was played by the search, the policy that beats greedy by 37.5 points. That is closer to how decks are actually piloted, but it is not proven: there is nothing to check it against, because TavernLab does not collect real winrates. Read it as a second opinion rather than as a corrected table.
meta.caveat_skipped: {n} deck(s) are outside this table because the simulator cannot field them: {decks}.
meta.caveat_small_field: The field is the gauntlet, not a ladder’s long tail. A deck that beats it is not thereby the best deck in the game.
